bullets.title: Futures red pre-open: Nasdaq -0.9% as AI rally pauses ahead of GOOGL/TSLA earnings
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures opened down ~0.4% and Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.9% Wednesday morning, reversing Tuesday's sharp chip-led rebound. Semi/memory complex broadly lower in pre-market (MU -4.5%, WDC -4.8%, INTC -4.0%, STX -3.8%), while Tuesday's close saw S&P +0.88% and Nasdaq +1.33% on AI momentum. GOOGL and TSLA report after the close Wednesday, with TXN and NOW also on deck.

bullets.title: Oil spikes to $91+ Brent / $87+ WTI as Hormuz transits hit zero and US-Iran war enters day 11
bullets.body: Brent crude surged above $91/bbl and WTI to ~$87.54 (+3.8%) as the Strait of Hormuz saw zero commercial transits and the US conducted its 11th consecutive night of strikes on Iranian military targets. Secretary of State Rubio cited Iran's 'lack of seriousness' in negotiations; Iran denied active talks but left message channels open. Roth estimates the war has cost $37.5B so far. Oil strength is pushing global sovereign yields higher and pressuring risk appetite into the earnings window.

bullets.title: Market concentration and breadth divergence at extreme historical levels — caution signals mounting
bullets.body: The 24 largest S&P 500 stocks now account for >50% of total market cap, the highest concentration in history and above the dot-com peak. Price-breadth divergence has occurred on 52 trading days YTD, already matching the full-year 2000 dot-com bubble total. Separately, semiconductors now represent 14% of total market cap — nearly double the dot-com peak — and the momentum factor hit its highest 3-month realized volatility in 45 years outside of recessions before its 11% bounce Tuesday.

bullets.title: 22V and JPM tactically bullish on Momentum/Growth/Tech into H2; key asymmetric risk is capex disappointment
bullets.body: 22V Research recommends long Momentum, Growth, and Risk-on factors in H2 2026 against a backdrop of benign real growth slowdown to ~2%, falling inflation, and easing AI EPS concerns. JPM is also tactically bullish and says it will flip bearish only if hyperscalers announce capex cuts or buyback reductions. Mag7 hedge fund L/S ratio sits at the 25th percentile since Jan 2018, suggesting positioning is washed out and supportive for upside.

bullets.title: GOOGL earnings bar very high: buyside expects Cloud +70-75% and 2027 capex $325-350B vs Street $250B
bullets.body: Google Cloud consensus growth is ~65% but buyside expects 70-75% Y/Y for Q2. JPM models 2027 capex at ~$300B (54% growth) vs Street ~$250B; buyside bar is $325-350B. AI debt issuance hit $489B YTD 2026 — already exceeding full-year 2025's $322B — and Google raised ~$85B in equity in June, signaling the shift from FCF to debt/equity financing of capex. Dealers are short gamma on upside strikes in GOOGL/META/MSFT/AMZN, which structurally favors long convexity into prints.

bullets.title: Jefferies warns AI capex returns increasingly debt-funded; risks circular vendor financing and capital destruction
bullets.body: Jefferies argues the top five US hyperscalers have accumulated $662B in off-balance-sheet future data center lease commitments not yet commenced, and are borrowing increasing amounts to fund AI capex. The firm warns virtually all AI capex arms-race value has been captured by picks-and-shovels semiconductor suppliers, and that LLM commoditization via cheap Chinese open-source models could trigger unwillingness to fund further hyperscaler capex — the 'long-term end game' being massive US capital destruction. Nikkei separately estimated $1.65T in off-balance-sheet GPU contracts, leases, and JVs across Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle.

bullets.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 launches with 10x token throughput vs Blackwell at same 150MW power draw
bullets.body: NVIDIA unveiled the Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale AI supercomputer on July 21, combining seven co-designed chips including the industry's first co-packaged optics (CPO) switch for scale-out networking — now described as in 'volume manufacturing.' CoreWeave benchmarks show 10x higher throughput per megawatt vs. Grace Blackwell NVL72. Wistron simultaneously opened a $700M, 324,000 sq ft Fort Worth, Texas facility producing GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra systems, with a separate production cell being prepared for Vera Rubin. NVIDIA Rubin (SM107) support was also added to PyTorch.

bullets.title: Taiwan June export orders surge 59.4% YoY to record $95.3B; TSMC plans ~10% price hikes from 2027
bullets.body: Taiwan's June export orders rose 59.4% YoY to a record $95.26B, well above the 47.3% expected, with electronics up 79.9% and IT/communications up 81.9%, driven by US demand (+83.6%). Separately, Nikkei reported TSMC plans to raise chipmaking prices by up to 10% from 2027 for advanced and mature nodes. VAT Group reported record Q2 orders of CHF500M (+35% vs consensus), a leading indicator for tool OEMs AMAT and LRCX, with book-to-bill of 1.7x.

bullets.title: BoJ signals openness to rate hikes faster than every six months; yen hits 39-year low at 163/USD
bullets.body: BoJ officials were reported open to accelerating rate hikes beyond the current every-six-month cadence, viewing recent yen weakness as an upside inflation risk. The yen fell to 163/USD — its weakest since the mid-1980s — while Japan's 10-year JGB yield rose to 2.75% (+3bps) and the 40-year yield touched 3.91%. Japan's June trade deficit widened to -¥406.9B (vs -¥120B estimate) as imports surged 25.4% YoY, driven by energy dependence.

bullets.title: UK June CPI prints soft at 2.6% YoY vs 2.7% expected; core holds at 2.6%, services at 3.6%
bullets.body: UK headline CPI fell to 2.6% in June from 2.8% in May, beating the 2.7% consensus and the BoE's own 3.1% forecast. Core CPI held steady at 2.6% (above 2.5% expected) while services inflation eased to 3.6% from 3.7%. JPM raised its Q4 2026 headline inflation forecast to 3.4% (from 3.0%) on higher oil/TTF assumptions ($85 oil, €55 TTF), suggesting near-term BoE breathing room but rising H2 pass-through risk. German 2-year yields hit a 2-year high of 2.82%, and French 30-year bond yields reached their highest level since the GFC.

bullets.title: Trump tariff escalation resumes: new levies on dozens of nations by Friday, 100% on generic drugs from 2028
bullets.body: The temporary 10% global tariff expires Friday and Trump is set to impose fresh tariffs on dozens of nations as early as this week. Separately, Trump announced a 0% tariff on imported generic drugs through August 2028, escalating to 100% for one year and 200% thereafter, aimed at reshoring pharma manufacturing. Section 338 tariffs on Canada are described by Morgan Stanley as having limited macro effect but rising strategic risks.

bullets.title: GPU supply constraints tightening: B200 availability at 0%, GH200 aggressively constrained post-Kimi K3
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm B200 GPU availability has fallen to 0% and GH200 availability is tightening aggressively following the Kimi K3 model release. The Chinese AI model's deployment is creating significant incremental demand. This dynamic is seen as bullish for NVDA hardware and the broader AI infrastructure supply chain including memory (MU) and optical components (LITE, AAOI).

bullets.title: US retail card data weakening: July MTD spending -2.2% vs June +1.4%; consumer decelerating
bullets.body: Citi credit card data for July MTD shows aggregate US retail spending at -2.2% (-2.6% ex-food), a sharp deceleration from June's +1.4%. The July weakness is partly due to a difficult YoY comparison (July 2025 was fiscal 2025's strongest month) and Amazon moving Prime Day to June, which pulled forward competitor promotions. Electronics decelerated -1,330bps MTD and Athletic Footwear fell -1,530bps, while Off-Price Retailers decelerated -1,730bps.

bullets.title: Moody's upgrades Argentina to B3 (positive outlook); all three agencies have now upgraded
bullets.body: Moody's upgraded Argentina's sovereign rating from Caa1 to B3 with a positive outlook, citing materially declined default risk, fiscal balance, disinflation, end of monetary deficit financing, and economic liberalization. Argentina is forecast to grow GDP 3.4% in 2026 and 3.5% in 2027. All three major rating agencies have now upgraded the country.

bullets.title: Fed rate hike probability jumps to 71% by September on oil surge and sticky inflation
bullets.body: Fed funds futures are pricing a >71% probability of a rate hike by September, up from ~15% a week ago, driven by oil's surge above $91/bbl and sticky core inflation signals. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.64% (+1bps) and the 30-year is approaching GFC highs. Hedgeye's QUAD3 framework (bullish oil and yields) is signaling bearishness for housing stocks and bullishness for REITs, software (BUG), and energy.

bullets.title: Open-source AI and token optimization: neutral-to-positive for NVDA/hyperscalers, bigger risk in software
bullets.body: UBS and multiple sell-side analysts frame the open-source model and token spend optimization debate as neutral-to-positive for Nvidia and hyperscalers (more deployments = more hardware demand) but a potential headwind for software vendors where token cost scrutiny could pressure spending. Piper Sandler notes infrastructure software (TEAM, MDB, SNOW) enable 50-75% token cost savings, creating demand. BofA's Vivek Arya notes open-source AI creates a new memory footprint with each deployment vs. closed models that concentrate HBM demand.

bullets.title: North America data center installed capacity hits record 75 GW in Q2, with 210 GW planned
bullets.body: JPM data shows North American installed data center capacity reached a record 75 GW in Q2 2026, up 13 GW sequentially from 62 GW in Q1. Planned capacity rose to 210 GW from 195 GW in Q1 and 116 GW a year ago. Data centers accounted for 46% of PJM's last four capacity auction costs, reflecting rapidly growing power demand. The strong demand and tight supply backdrop support continued AI infrastructure investment, benefiting hardware and networking suppliers.
